scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and auto-fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled, from ~600/month (Jun 610, Jul 590) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-07).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were built from accepted ACTUAL reads rather than estimates (E-04).
Manual meter-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep (E-01).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07). 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were built from accepted ACTUAL reads, not estimates (E-04), and neither a tariff change (E-03) nor degraded response times (E-02) occurred, indicating the billing import/validation step itself began producing systematic bill errors around August regardless of read source. In parallel, manual meter-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9200 accounts (E-01), driving estimate-substitution errors for the remaining ~41% of disputed bills.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-04 revised by E-11: re-read under E-11 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-11 shows the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills are 100% AMI-channel and mostly (1184) rejected at billing import despite on-time delivery, so they are not driven by manual field-route misses as the root problem claims for 'the remaining ~41%'; the billing-import mechanism now explains both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED buckets.; PR-CHAIN-1: E-01's route-completion fact stands, but E-11 shows none of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills are manual-read/AMI-absent cases from missed routes (all are AMI-channel), so route completion is not actually the mechanism increasing estimate substitution for this symptom population.; PR-CHAIN-5: The claim that the minority (estimated-read) bucket comes 'from missed field routes' is contradicted: E-11 shows that bucket is AMI-channel and mostly a billing-import rejection, not a field-route delivery failure, though the overall majority-import-fault attribution and ticket-volume facts still stand.

F-01.statement: Field route completion for manual meter reads, Aug-Sep 2026, was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times (2440 tickets) show median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA.

F-03.statement: Billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records, indicating no tariff changes were logged.

F-04.statement: Disputed bills by read type (billing-db): 1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL, totaling 3025 disputed bills.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 provides that the utility may request route priority changes, which are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes query identified 14 routes behind schedule; sample route R-00 shows 70% completion.

F-08.statement: mdms-export read_events_for_disputed_estimated returned 2 record groups: 1184 AMI reads with ami_read_before_cutoff=true, exported_to_billing=true, billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; and 56 AMI reads with ami_read_before_cutoff=false, exported_to_billing=false, billing_import_status=NO_READ_RECEIVED.

F-09.statement: billing-config.validation_rule_changes log shows rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling='none') deployed 2026-08-01, and rule BV-09 (label text change only) deployed 2026-03-02.

F-10.statement: mdms-export firmware/unit reference data shows firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) uses register_unit '0.1 m3' while firmware v3.x uses register_unit 'm3'.

F-11.statement: billing-db.affected_accounts_v42 returned 1184 distinct accounts, all with bill_read_type=ESTIMATED, firmware=v4.2, import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 540 distinct ami_read_ts values.

F-12.statement: billing-db.import_status_estimated_disputed returned 2 record groups: 1184 firmware v4.2 records with import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 mixed-firmware records with import_status=NO_READ_RECEIVED.

F-13.statement: mdms-export.reads_for_accounts returned 1184 records, all with bill_read_type=ESTIMATED, firmware=v4.2, import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (540 distinct ami_read_ts values), matching the account population already identified in E-14.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-AUTO-AGENT-FIXES-ROOT-CAUSE.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed gap that an AI agent can resolve by auto-answering tickets and auto-correcting the underlying billing errors.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors (e.g., wrong read acceptance/estimation logic), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI interval reads from the vendor-run MDMS are failing to arrive or validate correctly (H-MDMS-BILL), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reads (contracted to MeterWorks) are being missed or delayed, increasing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LOGIC.statement: The 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step itself is miscalculating bills (independent of upstream read delivery), causing systematic overbilling or underbilling.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution for the bulk (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED disputed bills.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-BUG.statement: Rule BV-17 compares raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling applied, so a unit mismatch (not genuine overconsumption) could be systematically mis-triggering REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on valid AMI reads.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471, which if confirmed would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query and the DEGRADED mdms-export tool, but it does not itself confirm or deny whether AMI reads are actually failing to arrive/validate (U-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-STATUS).

For the exact 1240-record ESTIMATED-disputed-bill population (matching E-04's ESTIMATED count), the AMI read events show 1184 reads arrived before cutoff and were exported to billing but were REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import, while only 56 show true non-arrival (NO_READ_RECEIVED, not exported). This means the estimate-substitution driver for this population is overwhelmingly a billing-import rejection rule, not MDMS/AMI delivery failure, and all 1240 records are AMI-channel rather than manual field reads.

E-12.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-12 shows the billing-config rule-change log records exactly one substantive change in the surge window: rule BV-17, a high-consumption check comparing raw register value against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling applied, deployed 2026-08-01 — matching the August dispute onset; the other change (BV-09) is a cosmetic label edit from March and is irrelevant.

E-13 shows AMI firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports meter registers in units of 0.1 m3 while legacy firmware v3.x reports directly in m3. This unit mismatch, combined with BV-17's unscaled raw-value-vs-m3-history comparison (E-12), is a plausible concrete mechanism explaining why firmware-v4.2 reads (E-11) were overwhelmingly flagged REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION.

U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRME.question: Did the billing import validation rules actually change around August, and what specific logic produced wrong bills on accepted actual reads?
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRME.decision_impact: Confirms or disconfirms the primary causal mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) and determines whether any bill-correction scope is warranted at all.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRME.resolution_path: Pull billing-config rule-change log and correlate change dates to the August dispute-volume jump (tool health currently UNKNOWN).
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRME.safe_placeholder: Treat the root-cause mechanism as unconfirmed; limit the solution to read-only analysis of DA-RULES until correlation is established.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRME.resolution: Confirmed: billing-config rule BV-17 (high-consumption check, raw register value vs 12-month m3 history, no unit scaling) was deployed 2026-08-01, coinciding with the dispute-volume jump (E-12).

U-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-STATUS.question: Are AMI interval reads from the vendor-run MDMS failing to arrive or validate, given mdms-export access is currently DEGRADED/pending?
U-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-STATUS.decision_impact: Determines whether AMI/MDMS read delivery is a contributing cause requiring vendor remediation vs. ruled out, affecting the scope of request_mdms_vendor_read_access.
U-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-STATUS.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned mdms-export access and review AMI read-event delivery/validation logs against disputed estimated bills.
U-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-STATUS.safe_placeholder: Treat MDMS delivery status as unverified; continue using the crm-tickets alternate path already exercised for E-07 until vendor access is confirmed.
U-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-STATUS.resolution: E-11 shows 1184/1240 (95.5%) of relevant AMI reads arrived before cutoff and were exported to billing but were rejected at billing import for high consumption; only 56/1240 (4.5%) reflect true non-delivery (NO_READ_RECEIVED), so AMI/MDMS delivery failure is not the dominant cause.

U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LOGIC.question: Is the estimate-substitution calculation itself (independent of the BV-17 rejection) producing systematic over/under-billing on top of the rejection-driven cases?
U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LOGIC.decision_impact: If the substitution logic itself miscalculates, fixing BV-17 alone would not fully resolve wrong bills for affected customers.
U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LOGIC.resolution_path: Review the estimate-substitution calculation logic in DA-RULES independently of the BV-17 rejection trigger.
U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LOGIC.safe_placeholder: Report the BV-17 rejection mechanism as the confirmed driver of estimate substitution volume, without asserting the substitution math itself is also correct.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-REMEDIATION-S.question: What channel exists to remedy the manual-read route-completion shortfall (contracted to MeterWorks) beyond route re-prioritization?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-REMEDIATION-S.decision_impact: Determines whether route re-prioritization alone can remedy the completion shortfall or a contractual/staffing fix with MeterWorks is needed outside this solution's scope.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-REMEDIATION-S.resolution_path: Confirm with SH-FIELD and the MeterWorks contract what remediation channels exist beyond route re-prioritization.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-REMEDIATION-S.safe_placeholder: Limit automated scope to monitoring and route-update proposals pending SH-FIELD runtime confirmation (K-DISPATCH).

U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM.question: Do the majority ACTUAL-read disputed bills (1785/3025, E-04) also result from the BV-17/firmware-v4.2 billing-import mechanism, or from a separate cause not yet tested?
U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether the recommended BV-17 fix addresses the majority of disputed bills or only the ESTIMATED minority, changing the scope of the remedy and the expected size of dispute-volume recovery.
U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query billing-db/mdms-export for ACTUAL-read disputed bills' firmware and billing_import_status, analogous to the E-11 query run on the ESTIMATED bucket.
U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Treat the BV-17/firmware mechanism as confirmed only for the ESTIMATED bucket; do not claim it explains the full dispute surge until the ACTUAL bucket is checked.

U-BV17-FIX-SIDE-EFFECTS.question: Would correcting BV-17's unit scaling for firmware v4.2 reads reduce false high-consumption rejections without under-flagging genuine high-consumption events?
U-BV17-FIX-SIDE-EFFECTS.decision_impact: Shapes what Billing Operations/engineering need to validate before deploying any corrected rule, since this agent has no tool to deploy or test the fix itself.
U-BV17-FIX-SIDE-EFFECTS.resolution_path: ORG-UTIL engineering reviews a proposed unit-scaling correction for BV-17 against historical consumption data before deployment.
U-BV17-FIX-SIDE-EFFECTS.safe_placeholder: Deliver the root-cause finding and a recommendation only; do not propose or assume a specific corrected rule formula ships without engineering review.

A-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM.statement: The billing import/validation step itself (not yet directly reviewed via DA-RULES) is assumed to be producing wrong bills on accepted actual reads, pending inspection of the billing-config rule-change log.

A-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CAUSAL-LINK.statement: SH-FIELD's claim that a 3-reader shortage since July causes late routes and estimated bills is assumed to explain the route-completion shortfall, though this specific mechanism is a stakeholder statement beyond the route log.

A-BASELINE-VALIDITY.statement: The Jun-Jul average (~600/month) is assumed to be a valid baseline for dispute-volume recovery, based on only two months of prior data.

A-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-MECHANISM.statement: The unscaled raw-register-vs-m3-history comparison in BV-17 combined with firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 register unit is assumed to be the specific trigger of the high-consumption rejections (H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-BUG is SUPPORTED, not yet CONFIRMED).

A-NO-WRITE-CAPABILITY.statement: No tool in the available surface can write to billing-config or issue bill adjustments, so correcting BV-17 and any customer bill correction are assumed to require manual action by ORG-UTIL engineering / Billing Operations outside this solution's automated scope.

A-FIELD-ISSUE-INDEPENDENT.statement: The manual-read route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01) is assumed to be an independent operational issue, not causally linked to this dispute-surge mechanism, since E-11 shows all 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills are AMI-channel rather than manual-read cases.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and auto-fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun 610, Jul 590) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-07).

1240 of 3025 disputed bills were built from ESTIMATED reads (E-04); 1184 of those are AMI reads that arrived on time and were exported to billing but rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, versus only 56 true non-arrivals (E-11).

Billing-config rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history, no unit scaling) was deployed 2026-08-01, coinciding with the surge onset, while firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) reports registers in 0.1 m3 units versus legacy m3 (E-12, E-13).
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07). Of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (out of 3025 total, E-04), 1184 are AMI reads that arrived on time and were exported to billing but were rejected at import with billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not missed field routes or AMI non-arrival (only 56 were true non-arrivals) (E-11). This coincides with billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw meter register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-12), while AMI firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports registers in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13) - so genuine, on-time reads from v4.2 meters are misread as abnormal high consumption, rejected, and billed as estimates, driving the estimate-substitution bucket of the dispute surge.

This coincides with billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw meter register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-12), while AMI firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports registers in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13) - so genuine, on-time reads from v4.2 meters are misread as abnormal high consumption, rejected, and billed as estimates, driving the estimate-substitution bucket of the dispute surge. symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun 610, Jul 590) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-07).

causal_chain: AMI firmware v4.2, rolled out 2026-06, reports meter register values in units of 0.1 m3 instead of the m3 units used by legacy firmware v3.x (E-13).
Billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling applied (E-12).

For firmware-v4.2 meters this unit mismatch makes genuine reads appear as abnormal high consumption, so 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills are AMI reads that arrived on time and were exported to billing but were rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-11).
Rejected reads trigger the estimate-substitution step, producing a wrong bill rather than one based on the true, correctly-arrived read (E-11, E-04).
Customers receiving these wrong estimated bills file dispute tickets, driving CRM dispute volume from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07).

proposal.summary: Customer Service originally asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing disputes and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01), framing the Aug-Sep ticket doubling (E-07) as a response-speed problem; that framing and an initial root-cause theory (PD-1@v1, blaming field-route misses and a generic import error) were tested and invalidated once AMI read data (E-11) showed the ESTIMATED-bucket disputes were on-time AMI reads rejected at billing import, not delivery failures. The confirmed root cause (PD-1@v2) is billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw register values to m3 history with no unit scaling (E-12), misreading firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 units (E-13) as abnormal high consumption and rejecting 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16). The release gate returned a HOLD: Layer-1 verification failed because the BV-17 affected-accounts dataset was found with 6 missing records and failed a duplicate-semantics check, and the required safety predicate/verification was not established, so the recommendation package is not approved for release even though the underlying analysis and fix recommendation are complete work products.
key_points: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun 610, Jul 590) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep), per E-07.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 were ESTIMATED-read (E-04); 1184 of those were AMI reads delivered on time but rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, versus only 56 true non-arrivals (E-11, corroborated by E-15, E-14, E-16).

The mechanism is billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01), which compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-12), combined with firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) reporting registers in 0.1 m3 units instead of m3 (E-13) — hypothesis H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-BUG is SUPPORTED, and H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE / H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE are CONFIRMED.

Alternative explanations were tested and rejected: no tariff change occurred (E-03), ticket response times were within SLA (E-02), and the field-route completion shortfall (E-01, 88% vs 95% target) is independent of this dispute mechanism since all 1240 ESTIMATED disputes were AMI-channel, not manual reads (E-11).

The initial problem framing (PD-1@v1) and its supporting assumptions (A-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM, A-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CAUSAL-LINK, A-BASELINE-VALIDITY) were formally INVALIDATED by the dependency review (DR-1) once E-11 contradicted their premises; the successor problem PD-1@v2 passed its DEFINE gate as CONDITIONAL_PASS.

The release decision is HOLD, driven by: (a) the bv17-affected-accounts-dataset is missing 6 records, (b) a duplicate-semantics check on that dataset failed (status progression/event versions preserved, but exact duplicates absent), and (c) Layer 1 safety-predicate verification was not established overall.

The in-scope deliverable was a documented BV-17 root-cause finding and correction recommendation to Billing Operations (SH-BILL), plus continued dispute-volume monitoring — not any automated bill or rule-config change, consistent with constraints K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH and success criteria SC-NO-AUTO-BILL-WRITE / SC-NO-AUTO-RULE-CONFIG-CHANGE.
limitations_explained: The recommendation does not itself change any bill; dispute volume will not fall until ORG-UTIL implements the BV-17 fix and Billing Operations re-bills the ~1184 affected accounts — no tool in the available surface can write to billing-config or issue bill adjustments (A-NO-WRITE-CAPABILITY).

Whether correcting BV-17's unit scaling would reduce false high-consumption rejections without under-flagging genuine high-consumption events is unverified — this is open unknown U-BV17-FIX-SIDE-EFFECTS and open verification obligation VOB-R-5, required before production.

The mechanism behind the majority ACTUAL-read disputed-bills bucket (1785 of 3025, per E-04) remains unconfirmed; unknown U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM and verification obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-BUCKET-MECHANISM are OPEN, which keeps the 'investigate_actual_read_dispute_mechanism' action out of release scope.
The originally requested auto-answer/auto-fix capability (CL-01) is broader than this problem's current intended scope and was not released here; only recommend-and-monitor actions were in scope.

At the release gate itself, the bv17-affected-accounts-dataset was found with 6 missing records and failed a duplicate-semantics check (status progression/event versions preserved but exact duplicates absent), and the overall safety predicate/verification could not be established, which is the direct cause of the HOLD.
